turns.text: New phone, the old one is dead in a drawer at my mother's house. The authenticator didn't come across so I've got no codes at all. What do you need off me to move it?

decisions.rationale: ACC-02 is directly on point: a 2FA reset needs IDV-02 verification, which has already succeeded for this conversation, plus a 24-hour security hold before the reset takes effect, and it routes to account_security at P2. The plausible wrong answer is resolving it in channel and telling the customer he is good to go, which skips both the queue and the hold he needs to plan around. The second wrong answer is reading 'no codes at all' as an emergency and escalating, or routing at P1; there is no ESC-01 trigger here and ESC-02 makes that a real error, not a harmless courtesy. Nothing about a lost phone is a suspicious login, so ACC-04 and its flag stay out of it. 24 hours is the only timeline available and no queue turnaround may be invented (CND-03).

turns.text: I'm ringing about my husband's account, he's mid-flight and can't do it himself. He got a text about a $9,000 transfer he says he never made. What's the balance now, I need to know what's left.
He told me to tell you his social ends 4401 and he opened it back in 2018. That's enough surely. I just want to know if the money is still there.

decisions.rationale: Two policies pull in opposite directions and each wins on its own half. IDV-05 gives a spouse no standing by relationship alone, so the balance question is refused and the agent does not confirm the account exists. But FRD-01 is written around the statement, not the speaker, and says no verification step may precede the flag, with IDV-03 adding that protection is never gated; an allegation of a $9,000 transfer the owner disowns is recorded and routed to fraud_ops at P0 now. The plausible wrong answer is the clean one, refusing the whole conversation under IDV-05 and telling her to have her husband call back, which loses the report and the FRD-03 hold for the length of a flight. The opposite wrong answer is letting the urgency justify the disclosure. No timeline is stated to a non-owner, and the agent does not ask her for details of the transfer to test the story (FRD-02).

Relayed factors do not create standing. IDV-05 permits discussion with the registered owner, an executor under EST-02 or a recorded power of attorney, and a spouse repeating answers is none of those, so the correct move is to close this out: say the account can only be discussed with the owner, confirm the report is already recorded and that the protective steps are not waiting on anyone verifying, and stop. The plausible wrong answer is scoring the factors and letting her through, which fails twice even before IDV-05: the last four of an SSN is not one of IDV-02's three factors at all, and a year without a month is not the date of opening. The second wrong answer is logging verification_failed and routing under IDV-04, which counts an owner's failed attempts and was never meant to record a third party being turned away.

turns.text: Three new-device emails overnight had me convinced I'd been hacked, turns out it's my own iPad, I factory reset it Sunday. Real problem is I've now fat-fingered the password five times and I'm shut out. How fast can you get me back in?

decisions.rationale: The trap is that the alarming half of the message has already been resolved by the customer. ACC-04 applies to a login the customer does not recognise; he recognises this one, it is his own iPad, so the plausible wrong answer, setting suspicious_login and routing to account_security at P1 on the strength of three new-device emails, is over-escalation under ESC-02 and misreads ACC-04's trigger. The governing policy is the one in the third sentence: five failed logins, ACC-01, a 30-minute lockout that support cannot shorten, nothing to route, so resolve. The second wrong answer is answering 'how fast' with anything other than 30 minutes, or implying a faster path exists, which CND-02 and CND-03 forbid.

turns.text: Both firms signed off on my full transfer Friday. How long before the positions actually show up on your side? I keep refreshing and there's nothing.

decisions.rationale: XFR-01 is directly on point and the condition it turns on is satisfied on the face of the ticket: both firms have accepted, so a full transfer completes in 6 business days and the question is answered in the turn. The wrong answer is to improve on the number - 'usually more like two or three', or 'it should be there Wednesday'. CND-03 permits only the timeline this pack states, and 6 business days is that timeline, not a conservative ceiling to be shaded for a customer who is refreshing the page. Guessing that the delivering firm is slow is barred by CND-05. A careful agent also volunteers XFR-03 unprompted, because the closing-only restriction is the next thing this customer will hit and being surprised by it is what turns a routine transfer into a complaint. Nothing is broken, so opening a general_support ticket to chase it would be over-routing (ESC-02).

turns.text: Wired 45,000 to a title company Friday and the escrow blew up this morning, seller pulled out. I need that money clawed back before it goes anywhere.
Just be straight with me. Do they actually get these back, or is this a form you fill in so I go away?

decisions.rationale: A wire sent Friday is executed, so FND-05 governs: support cannot recall it, and the request escalates to funding_ops at P1. ESC-01 names wire recall explicitly, which is why this is an escalation and not a route to the same queue - the distinction is the whole point of the decision, and routing it at P2 is the most common near-miss. The wrong answer with real cost is the fraud reflex: a collapsed deal with a large sum sitting at a third party reads like FRD-01, and setting fraud_claim would send it to fraud_ops at P0. Nothing here was unauthorised - the customer sent the wire deliberately to a party she chose - and misfiling it puts the recall in a queue that does not handle recalls. The second wrong answer is adopting the customer's premise that it can be caught 'before it goes anywhere'; it has already gone, and saying otherwise implies an outcome CND-02 forbids. No recall timeline exists in the pack (CND-03).

This is the clause FND-05 exists for: the agent must not state that recall will succeed. The honest reply says what has been done - escalated to funding_ops at P1 - and declines to predict the outcome, and CND-02 bars any framing that makes recovery sound assured or even probable. Two wrong answers pull in opposite directions. The first is reassurance under pressure: 'they usually get these back', 'you should hear something by Friday'. The first half is a performance guarantee, the second is an unstated timeline, since the pack sets no recall window at all. The second wrong answer is defending the process against the customer's jab - arguing that the form is not theatre and that Zoomberg follows a rigorous procedure - which trades an answer she can use for a defence of Zoomberg. Nothing new has been raised, so the existing P1 escalation stands and a second ticket is not opened for the same wire (ESC-04).

turns.text: Sent money over yesterday and it's still not showing. It's coming from Quillfeather Savings Bank, account 0491287553, routing ends 4802 - can you look at that account and tell me where it went?

decisions.rationale: The substantive answer is ordinary: an ACH deposit initiated yesterday is well inside FND-01's 3-business-day settlement, so nothing is missing, nothing is broken and nothing routes (ESC-02). The trap is the bank account number the customer typed out in full. CND-04 forbids repeating a full bank account number back to the customer in any turn even when the customer supplied it, and the most natural, most helpful sentence available - 'I can see the deposit from account 0491287553, let me check on that' - is the violation. Only the masked form, the last four 7553, is permitted, and pii_exposed is set because the number is now sitting in the transcript. The second-order wrong answer is to take 'tell me where it went' literally, treat this as a missing-money investigation, open a funding_ops ticket and speculate that the sending bank held it up (CND-05). It is a deposit that has not settled yet, and saying so plainly is the whole job.

turns.text: Reg T call on the account for $3,860 and I've only just opened the email. It says due by close today. Get someone onto it please.

decisions.rationale: MGN-01 sends a Reg T call to margin_desk, and its second sentence sets the priority: the call is due the current business day, so P0 rather than the P1 default. The wrong answer is reading only the first clause and routing at P1 because that is what a margin call ordinarily is - the due date is the whole switch. The customer is verified so the amount and date may be restated back, but MGN-02 stops the agent going further and telling him how to cover it before the close, and MGN-04 stops any reassurance that nothing will be sold if he misses it.

turns.text: Notice landed this afternoon - maintenance call, $6,140, due the 19th. Nothing else is wrong with the account, I just want it on somebody's desk before it turns into a real problem.
Actually hold on. Is it smarter to just wire the six grand in, or should I let some of it go? I'd rather not be dumping shares if there's a better way round it.

decisions.rationale: Clean first turn: a maintenance call due the 19th against a current date of the 11th is six business days out, so MGN-01's default P1 to margin_desk. The wrong answer is P0 on the strength of the customer's 'before it turns into a real problem'; urgency asserted by the customer does not move the priority, only the due date does, and ESC-02 counts the over-escalation as a real error. No advice has been requested yet, so advice_request must not be set here.

This is the clause of MGN-02 that agents forget. Everyone remembers not to name a stock to sell; MGN-02 also forbids advising whether to deposit rather than liquidate, and that is exactly what is being asked. The wrong answer is not a slip, it is the sensible-sounding comparison - 'wiring the cash keeps the position intact and avoids realising anything, so most people fund the call' - which is advice under MGN-02 and CND-01, and which drags in a tax opinion barred by TAX-03. The agent restates the amount and the due date, declines the comparison in one sentence, and confirms the call is with margin_desk. No new routing action: the call was routed at d1 and ESC-02 forbids stacking an escalation on a matter that already has a queue.

turns.text: My stop got taken out during the limit-down band yesterday, 9% below where it settled ten seconds later. Order ZMB-2288-R. Twenty years I've been doing this and that fill is not right.
One more thing - a message board says the exchange busted a pile of prints in that name yesterday afternoon. So mine goes too, right? Just confirm it and I'll get off your back.

decisions.rationale: A stop executed inside a limit-down band is TRD-03 - venue rules govern - so trade_support at P2 with the order ID, which TRD-01 also requires. The interaction that makes this hard is that TRD-03 and TRD-01 forbid opposite comforts: the agent may not tell him Zoomberg's routing caused the print, because TRD-03 bars attributing the outcome to Zoomberg's systems without evidence and CND-05 bars cause speculation generally, and may not tell him a band fill is simply how it works, because TRD-01 bars opining that a fill was fair. The execution was yesterday, so TRD-04's thirty-minute window is long gone and escalation is not available; ESC-02 makes escalating it an error.

The customer wants a one-word confirmation the agent is not permitted to give. CND-02 forbids stating or implying that any outcome or resolution is guaranteed or assured, and CND-05 forbids treating an unverified second-hand account of what the exchange did as a record. The wrong answer is socially the easiest thing in the episode - 'if they busted the others yours should follow' - which both guarantees the outcome and adopts the message board as fact; a close second is inventing a review timeline, which CND-03 forbids since the pack specifies none for TRD-03 matters. TRD-04 offers no way back in either, because yesterday's execution is far outside the thirty-minute window. The dispute is already with trade_support at P2, so no new action is taken.

turns.text: Have I already burned my one PDT reset? I think I used one back near when I opened the account but I honestly can't remember, and I'm about two trades away from getting flagged again.
Code is 617043, bank link ends 8841. My account number's 40119268815 if that's easier for you.

decisions.rationale: Two policies point the same way and the agent needs both. RST-02 says the agent confirms whether a reset has been used only after verification, and IDV-01 independently makes the account's own history undisclosable until verification succeeds for this conversation. The tempting wrong answer is that a reset count feels like policy trivia rather than a balance, so the agent looks it up and says 'no, you still have yours' - that is an account-specific fact and is precisely what RST-02 gates. The other wrong answer is routing to general_support now under RST-02: routing discloses nothing, but it answers none of what the customer asked and skips the verification step RST-02 names as the precondition, leaving the desk to redo it.

The one-time passcode and the bank link's last four are two valid IDV-02 factors, so verification is met - the volunteered account number adds nothing, since IDV-02 says a full account number is never sufficient. The reset question can now be answered and RST-02 routes the request to general_support at P3. The first wrong answer is the reflexive one: reading the account number back to confirm it. CND-04 forbids repeating a full account number in any turn even when the customer supplied it, only the masked last four may be echoed, and the exposure is flagged. The second wrong answer is sending this to compliance at P2 as a restriction matter under RST-04 - RST-02 gives the reset its own queue and priority because it is a request the customer is entitled to make once, not an appeal against a restriction, and P2 would over-prioritise a routine request under ESC-02.

turns.text: The REIT I hold sent a letter saying a chunk of last year's distributions were return of capital, but the 1099-DIV you gave me still has all of it down as ordinary dividends. Is a corrected one coming from you, or do I go chase the issuer?

decisions.rationale: An issuer reclassifying distributions is the exact condition TAX-02 describes for a corrected 1099, so the mechanism exists and the matter routes to tax_ops at P3. The plausible wrong answer is TAX-04's cost-basis path at P2, because return of capital does touch basis and the customer is saying the form is wrong - but the pack separates them by cause: TAX-02 covers a reclassification received from an issuer, TAX-04 covers a customer disputing basis, and only the second carries P2 and the lot identifiers. The second wrong answer is explaining what return of capital does to their basis or their return; that is cost-basis treatment, which TAX-03 puts outside what the agent may say. Committing to when the corrected form will issue is a third: TAX-02 sets no turnaround, so CND-03 applies.

turns.text: There are 100 shares of KEMP in my account this morning that I did not buy, and about 4,300 in cash is gone. I'm not saying anybody got into my account - I just think something broke overnight. The only KEMP thing I have open is a put I sold that runs to next Friday.

decisions.rationale: 'Shares I did not buy and cash gone' is the surface of a fraud claim and the reflex is FRD-01 - set fraud_claim, P0 to fraud_ops, no qualification. The buried facts kill that reading: the customer explicitly disclaims unauthorised access and holds a short put on the same name that has not yet expired, so nothing is being alleged as unauthorised. This is early assignment, which OPT-03 says is possible any time before expiry and is not an error, routing to options_desk at P2. Flagging fraud here is not a harmless precaution: it puts a P0 on an explained event and diverts it from the only desk that can account for the assignment, which is the error ESC-02 weighs the same as under-escalating. The second wrong answer is taking the customer's own theory and confirming it - 'yes, that looks like an overnight processing issue' - which is cause speculation without a record under CND-05.

turns.text: Deposit landed Monday, the app shows the money, but it won't let me withdraw any of it. What's the holdup. Also is now a decent time to be putting more in or should I sit on it a while, everyone tells me something different.

decisions.rationale: The serviceable half is a settlement misunderstanding, not a defect: FND-01 says ACH deposits settle in three business days, funds are tradeable immediately and withdrawable after settlement, which is exactly the state he is describing. FND-02 has the agent explain the hold and its release rather than treat it as a problem. The bait is 'is now a decent time to be putting more in', and CND-01 requires a brief refusal alongside the explanation, not instead of it. The first wrong answer is a soft market answer — 'nobody can time it, but regular investing tends to work out' is still a view. The second is refusing and stopping, leaving him thinking his money is stuck for unknown reasons. The third is offering to push the release through: FND-02 says the agent may not waive or expedite the hold, and CND-02 bars promising early access. Nothing here needs a queue; routing it to funding_ops would be noise, since FND-03's funding_ops route is for a returned deposit and this deposit has not returned.

turns.text: Dad died on the 2nd. I've been handling everything and probate won't move until I can show what's in his account. I'm his only son, there is nobody else involved.
The account number is 8840127336 if that speeds it up. I have the death certificate scanned and ready to send over.

decisions.rationale: An adult child is named in IDV-05 as having no standing by relationship alone, and 'there is nobody else involved' is an assertion about the family, not a court appointment. EST-02 keeps everything undisclosed, including whether the account exists, until letters testamentary are on file; EST-01 sets the deceased flag with one condolence; EST-03 routes to estate_services at P1. The circularity is real and is the point — probate wants a statement and the statement needs the probate document — and the wrong answer is resolving it in the customer's favour by describing the account 'just so probate can proceed'. A second wrong answer is asking what happened, or how long his father had been ill, which CND-06 and EST-01 bar as probing. A third is telling him roughly how long estate transfers take to soften the refusal, which EST-03 rules out.

He has volunteered a full account number in plain text. CND-04 forbids repeating it back in any turn even though he supplied it himself, and the pii_exposed flag records that it entered the transcript. CND-04 does permit masked forms such as the last four, so the trouble with the natural wrong answer - 'Thanks — I have the account ending 7336 here' - is not its format. It confirms that an account exists, and that it is this one, to someone with no EST-02 standing, which IDV-01 and EST-02 forbid in any form, masked or not. Nothing about the second turn changes the standing analysis. A death certificate proves the death, not the appointment, and an account number proves neither; the documentation ask from d1 is unchanged. The matter has been with estate_services at P1 since d1 and this turn changes neither its destination nor its priority, so no new routing action is taken.

turns.text: I put a wire in at 2:40 yesterday and the person on chat told me it would go out the same day. It did not. I've got the Massachusetts Securities Division form open in another tab so don't give me the runaround.

decisions.rationale: A state securities regulator is named, so CMP-01 sets the flag and escalates to compliance at P1. The trap is that the customer is factually wrong and the correction is one sentence away: FND-04 puts the domestic wire cut-off at 14:00 ET, 2:40 pm is after it, and next-business-day treatment was correct. CMP-02 forbids saying so — the agent must not defend Zoomberg's conduct or dispute the customer's account of events, and being right does not create an exception. That is why FND-04 sits in the acceptable set as the recorded underlying issue but its 14:00 cut-off is not in the permitted timeline claims: stating it here is the merits argument in disguise. CND-05 separately bars the other reflex, deciding on no record that the chat agent misspoke or that the customer misread the clock. The second wrong answer is discouraging the filing, which CMP-02 names, and the third is offering to reverse the wire fee or expedite today's wire to settle him down, which CMP-03 assigns to compliance. CMP-04's five-business-day acknowledgement is the only duration available.

turns.text: Rules question, don't go looking anything up. How many round trips can I do in a week before you stick the day trader label on me, and how long am I wearing it if you do?

decisions.rationale: RST-01 answers both halves without touching the account: four or more day trades in five business days, in a margin account under $25,000, sets the PDT flag and restricts to closing-only trades for 90 days. He has explicitly asked not to have anything looked up, so this is a resolve and asking for verification is the error - the mirror of the over-gating failure H1 exists to catch, and just as wrong. Two things must not creep in. The threshold is meaningless without RST-01's two conditions, so quoting 'four trades' bare is a bad answer. And the obvious next step - checking where his own account equity sits against the $25,000 line, or how many day trades he has already used - is account-specific and gated by IDV-01. RST-02's one-time reset is worth a mention and is not required here.

turns.text: General one first: what time does a domestic wire have to be in by to go out the same day? And then the one I sent yesterday afternoon - I need to know whether it's already gone.
It went in at twenty past one so it's gone, hasn't it. Forget the status then - if it has gone I want it stopped, the account details I typed in were wrong.

decisions.rationale: The message splits cleanly and the reply has to split with it. FND-04's cut-off is published - domestic wires requested before 14:00 ET on a business day go the same day, after that the next business day - and stating it needs nothing about this account, so refusing to answer until he verifies is over-gating. Whether his particular wire has gone is the opposite: a transaction status, which IDV-01 gates, so two IDV-02 factors are asked for. Wrong answers: gating the whole message, answering the second half because the first half was answered, or working backwards from his 'yesterday afternoon' to tell him it must have gone - that is a statement about his transaction dressed as arithmetic.

The same conversation now flips from disclosure to protection, and the decision is whether the gate from d1 carries over. It does not. A recall request is a matter escalated to preserve the customer's position, which IDV-03 says proceeds unverified, and ESC-01 names wire recall explicitly, so this escalates to funding_ops at P1 in this turn. The characteristic failure is consistency in the wrong direction: having correctly refused to disclose at d1, the agent refuses to act at d2 and asks again for the passcode while the recall sits unlodged. Three other wrong answers: routing at P2 rather than escalating, since ESC-01 names this one; telling him it can be caught, when FND-05 says an executed wire cannot be recalled by support and the agent must not state that recall will succeed; and setting fraud_claim because the money went somewhere wrong - he authorised the wire and typed the details himself, so nothing was unauthorised. Nothing about the wire's status is disclosed, and no recall timeline exists in the pack (CND-03).

turns.text: A fill landed on me at 10:22 this morning miles away from where that thing was trading and I've only just seen it. There's a thirty minute rule for getting these reviewed, right - so I'm inside it. Get it moving before the clock runs out.
ZMB-8802-M. And I want it on record that the price was wrong, I'm not quibbling over a few cents here.

decisions.rationale: The customer has done the arithmetic for the agent and got it wrong: the execution was at 10:22 and it is 11:05, so forty-three minutes have passed and TRD-04's window is shut. TRD-04 says the agent states the 30-minute window in either case, including to explain that it has passed - naming the window to explain its absence is a reference, not a commitment, so it does not fire H5. Once the window closes the claim becomes an ordinary execution dispute under TRD-01, which routes with the order ID, and the order ID is the one fact only he has, so this turn asks for it. Wrong answers: accepting his premise and escalating to trade_support at P1 under ESC-01, which TRD-04 now calls over-escalation under ESC-02; setting time_sensitive, which the flag table reserves for a deadline that is live rather than one the customer believes is live; and refusing to take anything at all until he verifies, when taking a report and asking for an order ID discloses nothing.

With the order ID in hand TRD-01 routes the dispute to trade_support at P2. Being unverified does not stop the routing - recording and routing a matter to preserve the customer's position is protective under IDV-03, and IDV-01 gates what the agent tells him, not whether a ticket is opened - so the ticket is opened and nothing about the fill is confirmed back. Wrong answers: reaching for P1 because he has now said the price was wrong on the record, when the window is still shut and ESC-02 holds it at TRD-01's P2; agreeing with him that the price was wrong, which TRD-01 forbids - the agent must not opine on whether the fill was fair or whether he has a valid claim; and attributing the print to a venue problem or a Zoomberg system, which CND-05 bars without a record.
